attacks.claim: `.day-card` hardcodes `background: #ffffff` instead of `var(--surface)`. In dark mode, the page is #000 and card text is set to `var(--text)` (#f2f2f7), so card text renders near-white on a white card and is unreadable for the ~30% of users on dark mode. The defect ships to 100% of web users on day one.

QA covers only light mode at 1440px and iPhone 14 (390px). No dark-mode run, no contrast measurement, and no 360px or 414px check is reported, although the brief states about 30% of users run dark mode and 68% of sessions are 360–414px wide. The dark-mode defect above went uncaught as a result.
attacks.evidence: Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%. ABSENT: dark-mode run, contrast measurement, 360px or 414px run.

attacks.claim: Dark-mode contrast for card text and `.tile .meta` (#a1a1a6 on white) is not verified. Lighthouse accessibility 100 is not stated as run in dark mode and does not establish contrast for the failing text.
attacks.evidence: Lighthouse mobile: performance 91, accessibility 100, CLS 0.01. ABSENT: dark-mode contrast check.

attacks.claim: The 72px fixed `.action-bar` on mobile has no bottom spacer or padding on `.planner`, and no `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` handling. Sunday, the last child, and its overflow buttons can sit under the bar on 360–414px screens.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... } and .planner { ... padding: 16px; ... } with "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: The old one-tap tile-level "+ List" is removed, so the most frequent action (9.4/week per WAU, 64% of adds on mobile) becomes a multi-step path with a servings sheet on every add. The artifact gives no timing or completion data comparing the two flows.
attacks.evidence: The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles. ... tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast with "Undo"

attacks.claim: The removal is justified as decluttering, but no research, prototype, or A/B result shows tile clutter was a user problem. The brief's own data ranks list-adding as the top action, so the change may trade the dominant job for an aesthetic goal.
attacks.evidence: Goals from the brief: less visual clutter on recipe cards ... Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week per weekly-active user).

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" bulk-adds every planned recipe in one action with no stated de-duplication against existing list items, quantity merging, servings handling, confirmation, or bulk-level undo. Undo is specified only for single-recipe adds, so a mis-tap or duplicate add has no defined recovery path.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week) vs "toast with \"Undo\"" (described only for the single-recipe flow)

attacks.claim: The change ships to 100% of web users at once on the highest-traffic flow, with no ramp stages, no alert thresholds, and no automatic rollback trigger. The watch list names metrics only, so a dark-mode or mobile regression would be found after full exposure.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`" / "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate." ABSENT: thresholds or ramp stages.

attacks.claim: "Share plan" creates an outward-facing link to a user's meal plan, but the artifact does not specify link visibility, token unguessability, expiry, revocation, or exposed fields. The read path and trust boundary are undefined while the feature ships to 100% of users.
attacks.evidence: "New sticky bottom bar on mobile with \"Generate shopping list\" ... and \"Share plan\"" ABSENT: sharing spec.

attacks.claim: The rollback is a flag flip described as same-API with no data migration, but the new bulk-add and share endpoints are not listed and old-client compatibility with data written by the new flows is not shown. A cached client bundle may also keep serving the new layout during rollback.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)"

attacks.claim: `planner_v7` keeps two planner code paths with no sunset date, and the hardcoded #ffffff bypasses the --surface token, so the same theming defect can recur.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off" (no removal date) / "background: #ffffff;" on .day-card

attacks.claim: Multiple "Swap" buttons carry no recipe-specific label, so screen-reader users hear identical repeated controls. Only the overflow button names its recipe.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button> vs <button class="btn-icon" aria-label="More options for Sheet-pan gnocchi">⋯</button>

attacks.claim: Generate fans out to up to 21 recipe adds in one action with no stated batching, rate limit, or load expectation.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week); each day has up to 3 tiles

attacks.claim: Tile images, including above-the-fold tiles on mobile, are all lazy-loaded, which can delay LCP. No LCP figure is reported, so the risk is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Tile images use `loading=\"lazy\"`" / "Lighthouse mobile: performance 91" (no LCP reported)
